source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text: Formative pruning in the young, non-fruiting years focuses on building the tree's permanent branch framework: remove low branches growing in toward the trunk or crossing each other, remove any second competing leader/central stem so the tree keeps one strong upright trunk, and select 4-5 well-spaced main scaffold branches radiating around the trunk to become the tree's permanent framework. Any dead, diseased, or storm-damaged wood should be cut back to healthy tissue and the cut treated with fungicide paste to prevent fungal entry, since open pruning wounds are a common infection point for durian's stem and collar disease pathogens.
